S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency service response within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, and submit a follow-up report with known causes and corrective actions within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours of identifying a material safety risk, and promptly provide updates and recommended precautions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% triggers a corrective-action plan submitted to regulators and retesting within 12 months. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically make a model ineligible for sale; regulators may impose proportionate interim safeguards or restrict sales where the manufacturer fails to meet its plan or evidence indicates an imminent serious risk. Manufacturers must provide complete per-model test results, including the test date and failure rate, to regulators and to customers who purchase that model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Newly installed systems must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote shut-off within six years of this standard taking effect, where technically feasible.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard is adopted.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, regulators must require a recall and manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers and provide required recall remedies.

document.section_notes: The final S2 gives per-model results to purchasers and regulators but has no permanent failure-rate cap or sales stop: exceeding 5% triggers only a corrective-action plan and retest, so the Hearth 10 (6.2%) is not barred. S5 sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no interim window, which would catch the Ember 8 (9.9), while S3 gives a six-year retrofit with an open 'where feasible' escape and S4 sets built-in suppression at 36 months. Overall the rules favour Northwind somewhat more than Halcyon.
